observed.facings.png: Three panels at one scale: south, east and north offline renders of the raised Timber drawbridge (Scrapper look). Each shows a flat dark pit rectangle on a tan ground, the raised leaf standing at the hinge bank, and pairs of rusty bollards with a tan rope coil lying on the ground beside each bollard. No rope spans the pit or reaches up toward the leaf.
observed.south.png: The raised leaf is a tall plank door with diagonal braces, iron corner plates and a dark hinge bar on the upper edge of the pit. Below the pit, two rusty bollards sit side by side. On each, a rope runs down the front of the post from the head into a squashed elliptical coil lying on the ground in front of the post foot. Zoomed in, each coil has an outer and an inner turn and a short loose end. No bollards show on the upper bank because the leaf hides them.
observed.east.png: The leaf is raised edge-on: a thin vertical plank with iron bands, its hinge at the west edge of the pit. Two bollards stand on each bank, west and east. Each has a coil lying flat on the ground on the side toward the pit, squashed about 2:1. Zoomed in, the coils show one and a half wobbly turns with a loose end running out across the outer turn; the west coils point the end east and the east coils point it west. The coils stop short of the pit edge. The top-left coil comes close to the leaf's hinge foot but does not overlap it.
observed.north.png: The leaf is raised over the pit, seen from the back: vertical planks with four iron straps, the hinge at the bottom edge of the pit. Upper bank (deck lies down the screen): two bollards, each with a coil on the ground ahead of its foot. The coil overlaps the bollard's base flange slightly in front, and no rope runs up the post. Lower bank (deck up the screen): the rope drops down the front of each post into a coil in front of the foot, like south. Each coil has two turns and a loose end at the lower left or lower right. The two coils of a pair nearly touch.
observed.scale.png: Context render of the lowered bridge (rotation E) beside a vanilla human. Taut ropes run straight from each bollard head across the deck rails. The bollards stand about knee-to-waist height on the human, and the deck is about three cells long.
observed.assembled_1.png: Same picture as north.png: raised, rotation N.
observed.assembled_2.png: Same picture as south.png: raised, rotation S.
observed.assembled_3.png: Same picture as east.png: raised, rotation E.
observed.assembled_4.png: Raised, rotation W: the mirror of E. The leaf stands edge-on at the east edge of the pit, and four bollards each have a flat coil on the ground toward the pit, with loose ends. The coils on the east bank lie just right of the hinge foot and do not overlap it.
observed.assembled_5.png: Context render of the lowered bridge (rotation N): straight taut ropes run from the bollard heads down to the deck at both ends.

CAMERA.seen: The coils are ellipses squashed about 0.5 in the screen vertical, which reads as rope lying on the ground plane. The bollards keep the approved building camera.

BORE.seen: No pipe or hose. The rope is solid and has no bore.

PORTS.seen: In the raised state the port is disconnected by design. Each rope starts at its own bollard (down the post front, or out of the foot) and ends in a coil on the same cell. Nothing reaches the leaf or crosses the pit.

PORTS_DRAWN.seen: Each bollard has exactly one rope or coil in every rotation (2 per bank, 4 visible in E/W, 2+2 in N). No extra connectors are drawn.

LAYERS.seen: Where the rope drops down the post front, it draws over the post. The coils draw in front of the post foot, and no far arc crosses behind the post. The raised leaf hides the south upper-bank coils, and none poke out at its edges.

ROTATIONS.seen: The same rusty bollard, tan rope and coil size and turn count appear in N, S, E and W. The 67% height spread comes from the bridge layout's canvas (the N/S pictures are long the pit's way), not from a pose change.

MATERIAL.seen: The coil uses the bollard picture's own twisted-rope texture, tan strands with dark twist lines, so it reads as hemp rope, not paint.

FOOTPRINT.seen: The coils stay on their bollard cells and on the bank, short of the pit edge, in all rotations.

ALPHA.seen: No shadow, ground patch or halo under the coils. The ground and pit are the render's context backdrop, not part of the part texture.

OURS.seen: The coils are cut from the mod's own bollard rope art and drawn by render_cables.py. No donor art.

OWNER_NOTES.seen: Slack and disconnected: no rope stands up as a hook or arch, and none spans the pit. True perspective plane (C6): the coils are squashed ground-plane ellipses.

LEGIBLE.seen: At 32 px/cell each coil is about 10 px wide and still reads as a pale ring at the bollard foot, distinct from the taut lowered rope. The loose end and inner turn are lost at that zoom, which is acceptable.

reply.subject: RM_SuspensionAnchor_Timber_Scrapper_slack
reply.image_seen: Image 1 compares three raised facings; 2 shows the braced leaf and lower coils; 3 shows the leaf edge and four coils; 4 shows the rear leaf between two coil pairs; 5 shows the lowered deck, extended ropes and human; 6–8 repeat the raised north, south and east views.

concerns.evidence: The raised coils show uneven nested turns and projecting loose ends crossing the outer turn, particularly clearly beside the east-facing leaf. The pairs reuse mirrored shapes, but variation between bollards is not required. Their flattened elliptical shape supports the required ground plane; they no longer read as single closed hoops.

In north.png and assembled_1.png, the upper-bank coils overlap the front edge of the bollard feet while the posts remain visible behind them. This matches foreground rope lying ahead of the feet. Partial flange occlusion does not show reversed layering.

The visible attachments are braided ropes with narrow loose ends. No pipe mouth or open hose bore is depicted in any raised view, so there is no visible bore facing an incorrect direction. The bore-plane check passes on the pictured geometry.

observed.facings.png: Three panels share one scale: S, E and N renders of the raised drawbridge. Each has a brown ground, a flat dark pit rectangle and the raised steel leaf standing at the hinge bank. Small dark-steel bollards with yellow-black hazard bands stand in pairs on the banks. Each bollard has a small grey rope ring lying on the ground beside or in front of it. The panels differ in shape (two tall portraits and one wide landscape) because the bridge runs along a different axis in each.
observed.south.png: The raised leaf (a riveted steel frame with three diagonal braces) stands upright on the upper bank above the pit, with a hinge bar at its foot. The upper bank's bollards are hidden behind the leaf. On the lower bank, two bollards stand side by side. Each has a dark rope strand running down the front of the post into a squashed elliptical coil lying on the ground just below the base, with the coil's far edge at the post foot.
observed.east.png: The bridge runs left to right. The raised leaf stands as a thin vertical steel beam at the left edge of the pit, with a hinge drum at its base. Two bollards stand on each bank. Each bollard has a flat ellipse of grey cable lying on the ground on the pit side. Each ellipse shows about one and a half turns: an inner turn, a slightly irregular outline, and a loose end crossing the outer turn and sticking out. On the upper-left bollard, the loose end points toward the leaf's hinge drum and nearly touches it.
observed.north.png: The bridge runs vertically. The raised leaf seen from behind is a riveted steel plate lying over the pit, with its hinge bar at the lower bank. Both banks have a pair of bollards. Each bollard has a rope strand dropping down the front of the post into a double-ring coil on the ground below it, with a short loose end at the lower edge. The coils are slightly wobbly but fairly regular.
observed.scale.png: Lowered state, context only, rotation E. The steel deck spans the pit with hazard-striped edges. Taut thin cables run from each of the four bollards to the deck edges. A vanilla human stands at the right and is clearly taller than a bollard. The lowered cable is as thin as the slack coil rope.
observed.assembled_1.png: The same picture as north.png: raised rotation N, with coils at both banks' bollards.
observed.assembled_2.png: The same picture as south.png: raised rotation S.
observed.assembled_3.png: The same picture as east.png: raised rotation E.
observed.assembled_4.png: Raised rotation W, mirroring E. The leaf stands at the right edge of the pit. The coils lie on the ground on the pit side of each bollard, with loose ends visible. On the lower-right bollard, the coil's end comes close to the leaf foot.
observed.assembled_5.png: Lowered rotation N, context only. Taut cables run vertically from the bollard heads to the deck ends. Bollards are on both banks.

CAMERA.seen: The coils are squashed ellipses lying in the ground plane, at roughly 0.45–0.55 of their width. The bollard tops show lit elliptical caps that match the building camera.

BORE.seen: No pipe or hose bore. The rope is a solid cable with no opening.

PORTS.seen: Each coil touches its own bollard. Where the deck lies up the screen (the lower bank in N and S), the rope runs from the bollard head down the post front to the coil. In E and W, the coil's outer turn meets the base. When raised, the ropes are disconnected from the deck, as specified.

PORTS_DRAWN.seen: Every bollard visible in every rotation has exactly one rope or coil. There are no extra connectors. In S, the upper bank's bollards are hidden behind the leaf, as the description intends.

LAYERS.seen: In the N and S lower bank, the rope draws over the front of the post. The coil's far arc stops at the post foot and never draws over the base. No coil pokes out from behind the raised leaf. The E coil end stops just short of the leaf's hinge drum.

ROTATIONS.seen: Every rotation has the same bollard, the same grey steel cable, and the same 1.5-turn coil with a loose end. W mirrors E.

SIGNATURE.seen: The raised state shows slack, disconnected rope lying in coils on the ground beside each bollard, with no upright hooks or arches. An inner turn and a loose end are now visible.

MATERIAL.seen: The rope has dark-and-light twisted-strand shading that reads as steel wire rope, matching the lowered cable.

FOOTPRINT.seen: The coils stay on the bank next to their bollards and never extend over the pit. The 67% height spread comes from the composite canvas shape (portrait N/S compared with landscape E), not from the subject.

ALPHA.seen: No halo or painted shadow is visible around the coils on the ground render. The offline renders are composited on ground, and the card's 'real alpha False' refers to those composites.

OURS.seen: The rope is cut from the mod's own bollard painting and placed by the mod's slack math.

OWNER_NOTES.seen: The ropes are slack and disconnected in all four raised rotations. The coils lie flat in the ground plane (C6). Nothing stands upright.

LEGIBLE.seen: At 1/4 scale, each coil is a roughly 12 px grey ring beside its bollard. It reads as a rope coil or loop, but the loose end and inner turn disappear at that size.

findings.seen: At standard zoom, the coil shrinks to a thin grey ring about 10–12 px wide. The inner turn and the loose end merge into a single hoop.
findings.quote: Textures are authored at about 128 px per cell; the player sees 32 px per cell in normal play
findings.fix: Each coil's cable is drawn about one pixel thicker at standard zoom, with the loose end extending a little further, so it still reads as a loose pile of rope at 32 px per cell.

findings.seen: The N and S coils are still two nearly concentric, fairly even ellipses. The hand-thrown wobble is slight, and the loose end is a short stub at the lower edge, so the coils read as somewhat neat.

findings.fix: The N and S coils show turns of visibly unequal size and offset centres, with a loose end that runs clearly out across the outer turn, like the E and W coils.

reply.subject: RM_SuspensionAnchor_Steel_Industrial_slack
reply.image_seen: 1: combined raised bridge facings with bollards and coils; 2: braced south leaf with two foreground coils; 3: edge-on east leaf with four coils; 4: plated north leaf with coils on both banks; 5: lowered striped deck beside a human; 6–8: repeated north, south and east raised views.

concerns.evidence: The north and south coils retain elliptical windings, but their lower edges show overlapping strands and projecting loose tips. The tips cross the outer winding and interrupt the closed-ring silhouette. The wobble is modest, but the inner winding and loose end requested for r4 are visible.

In east.png and assembled_3.png, a visible strip of brown ground separates the upper-left coil's rightmost tip from the hinge drum; that rope does not visibly connect to the leaf. However, the cited assembled_4 lower-right bollard is absent from the attachments, so that portion of the concern cannot be checked.

The visible ropes are thin solid strands forming ground coils; none depicts an exposed pipe or hose opening. The dark space inside each coil is the ground enclosed by the winding, not a bore facing the camera. No incorrect bore plane is visible.

edits.change: Each coil's loose rope end curls back across its own outer turn and finishes on the ground well clear of the raised leaf. It stops about one full coil-width short of the leaf's hinge drum, with bare bank ground showing between the rope tip and the drum.

On the bank where the leaf stands upright, the whole coil, loose end included, sits in the open ground in front of the bollard foot, inboard of the hinge drum. The rope reads as a free, unattached steel cable lying slack on the ground, separate from the leaf.

request.prompt: Top-down three-quarter painterly RimWorld sprite, vanilla RimWorld art style, realistic, clean dark outline, transparent background. Subject: the slack steel rope anchors of a one-lane drawbridge over a pit, shown in the RAISED state. The leaf stands upright at the hinge bank, and the ropes are disconnected from it and lie slack on the ground. Two upright steel industrial mooring bollards stand at each anchor square, unchanged from the approved bollard picture. Where the deck is up the screen, the thin steel cable drops from the bollard head down the post's front and ends in a loose coil lying on the ground just in front of the post, with the coil's far edge touching the post's foot. Nothing crosses behind the post. Elsewhere the coil lies on the ground ahead of the bollard foot. Each coil winds about one and a half turns, spiralling inward, so a second inner turn shows. The turns have a hand-thrown wobble, uneven in radius and spacing, like rope dropped by hand. The loose rope end runs out from the inner turn, crosses over the outer turn, and finishes lying on the ground. That end stops about one full coil-width short of the raised leaf's hinge drum, with bare bank ground visible between the rope tip and the drum. The whole coil, loose end included, sits in open ground in front of the bollard foot, inboard of the hinge drum, so it reads as a free cable lying slack and unattached to the leaf. Each coil is squashed in the screen vertical to match ground-plane perspective. In the N and S views the coils sit slightly inboard, so a coil behind the raised leaf stays hidden behind it. No rope lies over the pit. The cable stays as thin as the lowered steel cable, in dull steel grey with dark outline. The pit is a flat dark rectangle, the deck is a plain deck tile, and the raised leaf is drawn for context. reference: keep the previous render for the bollards, coil body and palette.
